reference: For parity cases, the reference branch uses GNU coreutils date with UTC epoch input (-d @SECONDS) and the same strftime format. This is independent of the builtin command path and gives GNU/POSIX conversion behavior under the runner's fixed C locale and UTC timezone. Contract cases use the stock loadable's published Bash help and usage synopsis.
coverage: Bash registration and published help text through type and help builtins
Known epoch timestamps with standard date, time, weekday, month, ordinal-day, and week-number conversions
ISO week-year boundary, leap day, 12-hour clock, GNU padding flags, literal percent, UTC zone, and epoch extension
Empty format and invalid timestamp diagnostics/status
exclusions: Current-clock numeric fields are not compared across separate executions; the omitted timestamp is covered with a literal format.
Non-C locales and timezone-database/DST transitions are outside scope; UTC and a POSIX fixed offset are covered.
Platform-specific strftime conversions beyond the selected GNU/glibc behavior and extreme timestamp limits are not covered.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash reports the compiled-in strftime command as a builtin, using Bash's type metadata contract.
Check that help exposes the long description documented by the stock builtin, including the optional epoch-seconds argument and current-time default.
cases.script:
h=$(help strftime)
if [[ $h == *"Display formatted time."* && $h == *"number of seconds since the epoch"* && $h == *"current time is used."* ]]; then
  printf 'documented help description present\n'
else
  printf 'documented help description missing\n'
  exit 1
fi

cases.purpose: Check that Bash help displays the builtin synopsis declared by the stock struct as 'strftime format [seconds]'.
cases.script:
h=$(help strftime)
if [[ $h == *"strftime: strftime format [seconds]"* ]]; then
  printf 'documented help synopsis present\n'
else
  printf 'documented help synopsis missing\n'
  exit 1
fi

cases.purpose: Compare standard calendar fields, names, ordinal day, weekday numbers, and Sunday/Monday week numbers for the Unix epoch.
cases.script:
format_at() {
  if [[ $(type -t strftime) == builtin ]]; then
    strftime -- "$1" "$2"
  else
    date -u -d "@$2" "+$1"
  fi
}
format_at '%F %T | %a %A %b %B | %j %w %u %U %W' 0

cases.purpose: Check that January 1, 2021 is formatted with the ISO week-year and week number that belong to the prior calendar year.
cases.script:
format_at() {
  if [[ $(type -t strftime) == builtin ]]; then
    strftime -- "$1" "$2"
  else
    date -u -d "@$2" "+$1"
  fi
}
format_at '%F %G-W%V-%u' 1609459200

cases.purpose: Exercise the final second of leap day 2024, including ordinal day, ISO weekday, and 12-hour AM/PM conversions.
cases.script:
format_at() {
  if [[ $(type -t strftime) == builtin ]]; then
    strftime -- "$1" "$2"
  else
    date -u -d "@$2" "+$1"
  fi
}
format_at '%F %T %j %u %I:%M:%S %p' 1709251199

cases.purpose: Compare space padding, no padding, explicit zero padding, and a literal percent at a date with a single-digit day and month.
cases.script:
format_at() {
  if [[ $(type -t strftime) == builtin ]]; then
    strftime -- "$1" "$2"
  else
    date -u -d "@$2" "+$1"
  fi
}
format_at '%e|%-d|%_m|%0H|%%|%F' 1706918400

cases.purpose: Check the UTC timezone name and offset together with the GNU epoch-seconds conversion.
cases.script:
format_at() {
  if [[ $(type -t strftime) == builtin ]]; then
    strftime -- "$1" "$2"
  else
    date -u -d "@$2" "+$1"
  fi
}
format_at '%F %T %z %Z %s' 0

cases.purpose: Verify an empty format succeeds and emits one newline, matching GNU date's empty output format.
cases.script:
format_at() {
  if [[ $(type -t strftime) == builtin ]]; then
    strftime -- "$1" "$2"
  else
    date -u -d "@$2" "+$1"
  fi
}
format_at '' 0

cases.purpose: Check that a nonnumeric seconds operand fails with a diagnostic and no formatted output, as GNU date does for an invalid @ timestamp.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t strftime) == builtin ]]; then
  strftime -- '%F' not-a-number
else
  date -u -d '@not-a-number' '+%F'
fi

cases.purpose: Check the documented seconds-since-epoch interface for timestamp -1, which GNU date formats as the second before the Unix epoch.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t strftime) == builtin ]]; then
  strftime -- '%F %T' -1
else
  date -u -d '@-1' '+%F %T'
fi

cases.purpose: Check the documented required format operand: an invocation without it returns the conventional EX_USAGE status and emits usage diagnostics.
Signed timestamps can cross a full day before the epoch.
cases.script: if [[ $(type -t strftime) == builtin ]]; then strftime '%F %T' -86401; else date -u -d '@-86401' '+%F %T'; fi

cases.purpose: Exercise the omitted-timestamp path with a format independent of the wall clock.
Compare an explicit POSIX fixed-offset timezone at epoch zero without timezone-database dependencies.
cases.script:
export TZ=UTC-5
if [[ $(type -t strftime) == builtin ]]; then strftime '%F %T %z' 0; else date -d '@0' '+%F %T %z'; fi
